advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile heal loop spend accounting so an admitted criterion is charged once (either let run_admission own the finalize, or point run_admission at a throwaway/separate ledger and let _record_spend be the single source of truth).
evidence: heal.py:382 `summary = _run_admission(criterion_id, rows, self._repo_root, self._ledger_path, self._cap_usd)` passes the same ledger_path the outer loop uses

solve() in _run_admission returns `CaseOutcome(fired=..., usage_rows=[])`, so run_admission's finalize prices an empty list (usd=0.0) — a $0 `admission-` entry plus a `heal-` estimate entry per admitted criterion
advisory.finding: In a live sweep the ledger is charged twice per admitted criterion: fixture_admission.run_admission (invoked via _run_admission with the same ledger_path) writes an `admission-<prompt_id>` finalize entry, and the heal loop's _record_spend then appends a second `heal-<prompt_id>` charge for the same attempt. Because the production solver returns usage_rows=[], run_admission's finalize prices an empty row list to usd=0.0, so a spurious $0 admission entry is written alongside the heal estimate entry — duplicate/inconsistent ledger accounting for the same attempt.

evidence: heal.py `_run_admission` calls `fixture_admission.run_admission(... ledger_path=ledger_path ...)` on the same ledger file the loop resets and reserves against
fixture_admission.py:224 `ledger.finalize('admission-{prompt_id}', ...)` writes an entry on admit
heal.py `_record_spend` writes an entry for EVERY attempt via finalize/charge_estimate on the same ledger_file
The solver comment states the priceable usage row is 'tracked as follow-up work'; when resolved, both writers become non-empty and double-count
advisory.finding: `_run_admission` passes the SAME `ledger_path` used by the outer heal loop and internally calls `ledger.finalize(...)` on each admitted criterion, while `_record_spend` in the heal loop independently records spend for every attempt. Today this is single-charged only because the production solver returns `usage_rows=[]` (admission finalize prices $0 and _record_spend charges the estimate). If the documented follow-up makes the case runner surface priceable usage rows, admission's finalize will record actual cost AND `_record_spend` will also record (its AttemptResult.usage_rows would then be populated), double-counting each admitted criterion against the cap.

evidence: heal.py `_gap_ids` returns `list(_default_criteria(str(repo_root), gate_key))` with no guard on emptiness
An empty `gap_ids` yields empty `attempted`; the loop body never executes and HealReport(ran=True) is returned as success
Litmus: 'the routing/registry produced nothing' and 'every criterion already has a spec' both yield the identical empty-attempt success verdict
advisory.finding: When the gap source returns an empty list (e.g. effective_routing / plan-review registry misconfiguration or all criteria already covered), the sweep computes an empty attempt list, advances the due-stamp, and returns HealReport(ran=True) with no admitted/quarantined entries — a success verdict indistinguishable from 'the routing failed to produce any criteria'. There is no assertion that the gap source actually ran and produced a non-degenerate result.

dropped.finding: The ADMITTED counter-reset contract clause ('reset the criterion's failure counter to 0') has no test. AC2 proves three consecutive failures quarantine, but no test drives fail→fail→ADMITTED→fail and asserts the criterion is NOT quarantined on that fourth run — i.e. that the admission cleared the accrued two strikes. If `_fold_outcome` failed to reset the counter (or reset the wrong key), the suite would stay green.

evidence: heal.py: `counters = {criterion: int(state["counters"].get(criterion, 0)) for criterion in attempted}`
Contract docstring: `Counters for criteria no longer in the attempt list are dropped (so a covered or quarantined — or reopened — criterion starts fresh).`
No test in test_fixture_heal_heldout.py exercises a criterion leaving and re-entering the attempt list; grep for 'drop' returns only an unrelated emitter comment.
dropped.finding: The 'counters for criteria no longer in the attempt list are dropped' contract clause is untested. The loop rebuilds `counters` only for the current `attempted` set, so a criterion that leaves the gap (covered, quarantined, or reopened) is meant to start fresh — but no test asserts that a criterion which accrued strikes, then left the attempt list, and later re-entered, restarts from zero.
